metadata.title: Collective Flourishing & Deep Time
metadata.notes: The high-level humanistic layer for long-term civilizational stability.

nodes.title: Bio-Regional Citizenship
nodes.description: Moving from human-centric to bio-centric governance. Understanding the local watershed and flora as citizens with rights. Implementing the 'Council of All Beings' in local DAOs.

nodes.title: The Anthropology of Gifts
nodes.description: Study of non-extractive economic systems: Potlatch, Kula Ring, and the role of 'Debt' as a social tether. Philosophical grounding for the TEND mutual credit system.

nodes.title: Collective Aesthetics
nodes.description: How beauty creates social coherence. Public art, shared rituals, and the role of 'Cultural Mycelium' in binding a decentralized network together.

nodes.title: The 7th Generation Principle
nodes.description: Deep Time Ethics: decision-making across centuries. Long-term stewardship of soil, knowledge, and cryptographic keys. The philosophy of 'Being a Good Ancestor'.

nodes.title: The Flourishing Masterpiece
nodes.description: Design and execute a project that satisfies the needs of both the human community and the local ecosystem. Must prove long-term viability (Deep Time) and social reciprocity.

holonic_capstone.deliverable: A multi-decade stewardship plan and a physical intervention (e.g., habitat restoration or community foundation) with a 50-year maintenance commitment.

edges.rationale: Flourishing requires the inclusion of non-human biological actors.
Real-world projects must be grounded in non-extractive gift dynamics.
The masterwork of a Type 1 Civilization must withstand Deep Time.
Deep ecology is a natural progression from Indigenous Knowledge Systems.
